speaker: Unknown
en: But first, maybe some of the problems that inspire us as a company at a bridge.

speaker: Unknown
en: One, one of the things that we've noticed, or many people, economists have noticed over the past few decades is actually, in many other industries, you actually see the cost of a good go down.
zh: 第一，我们注意到的一件事，或者过去几十年许多经济学家注意到的事情是，实际上，在许多其他行业中，你会看到商品的成本在下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's because the productivity has increased.
zh: 那是因为生产率提高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in healthcare, we actually see administrative costs have only gone up over the past few decades.
zh: 但在医疗保健领域，我们看到行政成本在过去几十年里只升不降。

speaker: Unknown
en: And productivity hasn't necessarily increased.
zh: 而生产率并不一定提高了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of our problems in healthcare we solve with labor, but even that we cannot actually keep up.
zh: 医疗保健中的很多问题我们是靠人力解决的，但即便是人力，我们实际上也跟不上了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's this bit of this like productivity paradox you might have heard of like Ballmer's cost disease.
zh: 所以存在这种你也许听说过的生产率悖论，比如 Ballmer 的成本病。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's partially because technology I think hasn't fully touched healthcare as much as it's touched other industries to increase that productivity.

speaker: Unknown
en: A few other problems, you know, hospitals are shutting down.

en: So what we started as a company was working on clinical documentation.

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea here, if you're not familiar with it, is at the end of every patient visit, the clinician must create a note.
zh: 这里的想法，如果你不熟悉的话，是在每次病人就诊结束时，临床医生必须创建一份病历记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our typical format is a SOAP note that has a couple different formats, like what's the chief complaint of the patient, and a few other sections, and then what's the assessment plan?
zh: 我们的典型格式是 SOAP 记录，它有几种不同的部分，比如病人的主诉是什么，还有其他几个部分，然后是评估计划是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do we do with this patient?
zh: 我们要对这个病人做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to write this after every single visit.
zh: 你必须在每一次就诊后写这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's some different variations on this depending on specialty.
zh: 根据专科不同，这也有一些不同的变体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Typically, clinicians end up often doing, it takes like two hours a day to just write these notes, and you often do it what's known as pajama time after work itself.
zh: 通常，临床医生最终往往每天要花大约两个小时专门写这些记录，而且你经常在下班后做这件事，也就是所谓的“睡衣时间”。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a common source of clinician burnout, spending all this time outside of work, and it's not the most fun part of the job.
zh: 这是临床医生倦怠的一个常见来源，在工作之外花费所有这些时间，而这并不是这份工作最有趣的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, these documents are actually extremely high stakes because these clinical notes are often used as a basis of billing, but also, which is, of course, financial things are high stakes, but also have clinical impact.
zh: 然而，这些文档实际上风险极高，因为这些临床记录常常被用作计费的依据，当然，财务上的事情风险很高，但它同时也有临床影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for this is because these notes are used for the next clinician or as you switch health systems.

speaker: Unknown
en: They provide context to the clinician

speaker: Unknown
en: Patient's Longitudinal Medical Record.

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's actually really high stakes to get this right.

speaker: Unknown
en: We started here because it's a known pain point that's existed for many, many years.

speaker: Unknown
en: But finally, the technology's caught up to do really, really high quality medical notes that's actually personalized to the clinician.

speaker: Unknown
en: This was an amazing wedge into healthcare industry, which has typically been technology reticent because they actually care a lot about getting these notes high quality and right.
zh: 这是进入医疗保健行业的一个绝佳楔子，这个行业通常对技术持保留态度，因为他们实际上非常在意把这些记录做得高质量、做正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: It led to higher provider satisfaction in such that they could actually see more patients.
zh: 它带来了更高的提供者满意度，因为他们实际上可以看更多的病人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it can actually help create a higher record that helps prevent as it relates to billing, auditing, and other reasons.
zh: 而且它实际上可以帮助创建一个更高的记录，有助于在计费、审计以及其他方面起到预防作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started there.
zh: 所以我们从那里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just this product alone scaled to 300 hospital systems.

speaker: Unknown
en: But I want to show you a little about where we're going next.
zh: 但我想给你展示一点我们接下来要去哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the core thesis of the company is that everywhere in healthcare, everything is around the conversation.

speaker: Unknown

en: Everything else is downstream of that, whether it relates to billing, whether it relates to things like clinical trial matching, or whether it relates to clinical decision support.

speaker: Unknown
en: It's all about the conversation, that sacred doctor and patient conversation, and we've just built all this administrative machinery around that.
zh: 一切都围绕对话，那场神圣的医生与患者的对话，而我们只是围绕它构建了这一整套行政机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: But how can we bring it back to that conversation and actually automate some of that administrative machinery?

zh: 我们面临的一些关键技术工程问题，并用我认为非常属于前沿 AI 挑战的一些内容来启发你们。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you've ever worked on a agentic product before, regardless of vertical, the three KPIs that tend to matter are quality and latency and cost.
zh: 所以如果你曾经做过智能体产品，无论哪个垂直领域，通常重要的三个 KPI 是质量、延迟和成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: In healthcare, I feel that we're actually playing on hard mode for all of these three KPIs.
zh: 在医疗领域，我觉得我们实际上在这三个 KPI 上都在玩困难模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a high-stakes scenario, especially when you're doing something like clinical decision support.
zh: 这是一个高风险场景，尤其是当你在做临床决策支持这样的事情时。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be right, because the downside is extremely high when you're wrong.
zh: 你必须是对的，因为当你出错时代价极其高昂。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I used to work at Glean, while I love that product, I could be wrong, and it would have been fine.
zh: 我以前在 Glean 工作时，虽然我热爱那个产品，我可能出错，但那没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we answered a question incorrectly.
zh: 也许我们回答错了一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in healthcare, if we answer something incorrectly, there's actually consequences, and we entirely lose our trust.
zh: 但在医疗领域，如果我们答错了什么，是会有真实后果的，我们会完全失去信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: So quality needs to be absolutely high.
zh: 所以质量必须绝对高。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll talk a little about how we keep that bar high.
zh: 我会稍微谈谈我们如何保持那个高标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then latency and cost also really matter for us when you're live in the conversation.
zh: 而且延迟和成本对我们也非常重要，当你处于实时对话中时。

speaker: Unknown
en: With latency, you can't act on information too late, and you have to act also at the right time for it to be useful.
zh: 关于延迟，你不能太晚才对信息采取行动，而且你还必须在正确的时机行动，它才有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And finally, cost at the scale we're doing this at.
zh: 最后是成本，在我们做这件事的规模下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as an interesting aside, it actually relates to, we have a motto inside the company that our goal is to save lives, save time, save money for the hospital system and for the healthcare industry as a whole.
zh: 作为一个有趣的题外话，它实际上与——我们公司内部有一个座右铭，我们的目标是为医院系统和整个医疗行业拯救生命、节省时间、节省金钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it actually, I think it's funny that it really maps to the three KPIs that you care about in any agentic product.
zh: 而且我觉得很有意思的是，它恰好对应任何智能体产品中你在乎的那三个 KPI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So talking a little about quality, how do we keep that bar high?
zh: 那么稍微谈谈质量，我们如何保持那个高标准？

speaker: Unknown
en: For us, we really treat evals as the operating system, the life's blood of the company.
zh: 对我们来说，我们真正把 evals 当作操作系统，当作公司的命脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: This starts from internal benchmarks and offline evaluation.
zh: 这始于内部基准测试和离线评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before we develop any product, whether we're talking about clinical trial matching, clinical note, clinical decision support, coding, we start with a robust set of internal benchmarks.
zh: 在我们开发任何产品之前，无论是临床试验匹配、临床记录、临床决策支持还是编码，我们都从一套稳健的内部基准开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is pre-deployment.
zh: 这是部署之前的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we test that against things that we've actually seen in the wild.
zh: 然后我们用它对照我们在真实世界中实际见过的东西进行测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we have a staged rollout.
zh: 接着我们进行分阶段推出。

speaker: Unknown
en: We know that we need to make contact with the reality.
zh: 我们知道我们需要与现实接触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everything offline will perfectly represent what happens in practice.
zh: 并非所有离线的东西都能完美代表实际发生的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we slowly roll it out.
zh: 所以我们慢慢推出。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe it starts with the alpha group of clinicians that we trust and understand the stakes.
zh: 也许从我们信任并理解其中利害的那一小批临床医生(alpha 组)开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We rely to beta.
zh: 我们依赖于 beta。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe there's A-B testing at scale.
zh: 也许会有大规模的 A-B 测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then even after it's fully rolled out, you always need continual monitoring.
zh: 而且即使在全面上线之后，你也需要持续的监控。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, the stakes are really high, and you cannot get away with just being like a prototype that you just ship out there and be like, yeah, I mean, I tested on a few cases and it works.
zh: 再说一次，利害真的非常高，你不能只是像个原型那样直接发出去，然后说，yeah,我是说，我在几个案例上测试过，它没问题，这样是行不通的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How we do this is we always have expert calibrated LM judges.
zh: 我们的做法是，我们始终有经过专家校准的 LM judges。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have clinicians embedded throughout the entire company.
zh: 所以我们的临床医生遍布整个公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The clinicians are domain experts, but not all of us are clinicians.
zh: 这些临床医生是领域专家，但我们并非所有人都是临床医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not a clinician.
zh: 我不是临床医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how can the rest of the company still move fast is by encoding that clinician judgment into LM judges.
zh: 那么公司其他人如何还能快速迭代呢？方法就是把临床医生的判断编码进 LM judges。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I think a really great evaluation system has a property that it reflects the behaviors that you want in your product.
zh: 你知道，我认为一个真正出色的评估系统有一个特性：它反映了你在产品中想要的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, we are making a product for clinicians.
zh: 说到底，我们是在为临床医生做产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so who best, other than our clinicians, to actually create our judges that represent what they want?
zh: 那么除了我们的临床医生之外，还有谁能最好地创建真正代表他们想要的 judges 呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And those judges, once you have that, create a feedback loop so that anyone, whether you're a clinician or not, can actually hill climb and learn from that.
zh: 而这些 judges,一旦你有了它们，就形成了一个反馈闭环，让任何人，无论你是不是临床医生，都能据此爬山并学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also have a lot of online signals, whether how you're editing the clinical note and your typical thumbs up, thumbs down, and star ratings and other free form text.
zh: 我们还有大量在线信号，比如你如何编辑临床记录，还有典型的点赞、点踩、星级评分以及其他自由文本。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a general framework we use for all our products.
zh: 这是我们所有产品使用的通用框架。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to deep dive into the product that I work on, which is clinical decision support.
zh: 我想深入讲讲我负责的产品，也就是临床决策支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to give you an example of what clinical decision support looks like, and specifically, we're building something novel, which is contextual clinical decision support.
zh: 给大家举一个临床决策支持的例子，具体来说，我们正在构建一些新颖的东西，叫做情境化临床决策支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe a provider asks a question like, hey, does this patient meet the criteria for fibril neutrophenia?
zh: 也许一个医疗服务者会问这样的问题：hey,这个病人是否符合 fibril neutrophenia 的标准？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we have to do here is actually a lot of context is underspecified in this question.
zh: 而我们在这里要做的，是这个提问中有很多上下文是没有明确说明的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first thing we're going to do is we're actually going to pull from the EHR data previous lab values.
zh: 所以我们要做的第一件事，实际上是从 EHR 数据里拉取以往的化验值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then using that context, we're also going to use live conversation and we're going to use clinical guidelines and medical journals to use as the reasoning sources for combining all this context to actually answer the provider's question.
zh: 然后利用那个上下文，我们还会使用实时对话，并且会使用临床指南和医学期刊，作为整合所有这些上下文来真正回答医疗服务者问题的推理来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, but I want to focus on evaluation.
zh: 现在，但我想聚焦在评估上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, the stakes are really high here.
zh: 再说一次，这里利害真的非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really can't get this wrong.
zh: 我们真的不能搞错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do you tell whether or not an answer is correct?
zh: 那么，你怎么判断一个答案是否正确？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a case where the generator and the verifier gap is really small.
zh: 这是一个生成器与验证器差距非常小的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I mean by this is in some problems in AI, such as Sudoku, it's really, really hard to generate a solution to Sudoku.
zh: 我的意思是，在某些 AI 问题里，比如数独，生成一个数独的解真的非常非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's extremely easy to verify.
zh: 但验证却极其容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you do have the solution.
zh: 一旦你有了那个解。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that makes it much easier to hill climb against and build evaluation for.
zh: 这使得对照它进行爬山以及构建评估要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in a case like this, the generator and verifier gap is really small.
zh: 但在像这样的情况下，生成器与验证器的差距非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I had a really, really good generator, verifier, then that would just be my generator itself.
zh: 如果我有一个非常非常好的生成器验证器，那它本身就是我的生成器了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do I create a reference that isn't just a language model itself and ground itself so I have trust?
zh: 那么我怎么创建一个不只是一个语言模型本身的参照，并让它扎根，从而让我能信任它？

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we do is we tackle this by having many, many different signals.
zh: 所以我们的做法是，用非常非常多的不同信号来应对这个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a clinical quality judge, which I'm going to dive deep into.
zh: 我们有一个临床质量 judge,我接下来会深入讲它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we tackle from we have many signals from a boundary and adversarial judge.
zh: 然后我们还从另一个角度入手，有很多来自边界与对抗 judge 的信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a clinical safety judge.
zh: 我们有一个临床安全 judge。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also have judges that represent product aspects like tone and style.
zh: 我们还有代表产品层面(比如语气和风格)的 judges。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that matters a lot as well for AI products.
zh: 这对 AI 产品来说也非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So all of these are different signals that try to get a piece of this really, really hard to measure problem and guarantee it in the way that we want the product to be.
zh: 所有这些都是不同的信号，试图去捕捉这个非常非常难衡量的问题的各个方面，并以我们希望产品呈现的方式来保证它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So diving into the clinical quality judge.
zh: 那么深入讲讲临床质量 judge。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, I said the generator verifier gap is really small here.
zh: 再说一次，我说过这里的生成器验证器差距非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we need is we actually need human references to tell are we generating the right thing.
zh: 所以我们需要的是，我们实际上需要人类参照来判断我们生成的东西对不对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can't just create a human golden response because there is a lot of variability in the potential responses.
zh: 但你不能直接创建一个人类的黄金答案，因为潜在答案存在很大的变异性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we did is we took a lot of real clinical cases.
zh: 所以我们做的是，取了大量真实的临床案例。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had independent physicians create a rubric.
zh: 我们让相互独立的医生制定评分细则(rubric)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this rubric said elements of what we wanted in the response.
zh: 这个细则列出了我们希望在回答中看到的要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not here's the exact response because, again, there's many infinite possible responses, but a good rubric elements that what a good response would look like.
zh: 它不是“这是标准答案”，因为再强调一次，可能有无穷多种回答，而是一份好的细则列出了好的回答应该是什么样子的要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we had a separate physician that actually adjudicated it, brought these two independent rubrics together, created a final rubric, and we actually had a fourth clinician do QA on these rubrics.
zh: 然后我们让另一位医生来仲裁，把这两份相互独立的细则整合在一起，形成最终细则，而且我们实际上还让第四位临床医生对这些细则做了 QA。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once you have these rubrics, and here's a sample rubric what it looks like.
zh: 一旦你有了这些评分标准，这里有一个评分标准的样例，它大概长这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's actually a question, and there's more context in the case itself.
zh: 这里其实是一个问题，案例本身里有更多上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a rubric of what are the elements that a response should look like.
zh: 你有一份评分标准，列出回答应该包含哪些要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now we can actually have an LLM judge that compares our agents' responses to these rubric elements and does some basic semantic match to tell, hey, is our model performing well as we continue to hill climb whether it's our agent architecture, our models, or search ranking algorithms.
zh: 现在我们实际上可以用一个 LLM 评委，把我们智能体的回答与这些评分要素进行比对，做一些基本的语义匹配，来判断：嘿，当我们持续爬山优化时——无论是智能体架构、我们的模型，还是搜索排序算法——我们的模型表现是否良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk a little now about cost and latency, two other really, really hard problems for us.
zh: 我现在想稍微谈谈成本和延迟，这是对我们来说另外两个非常非常难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do this, as we said in that intro video, we do this live in the conversation, and we do on the run rate of 100 million medical conversations a year.
zh: 就像我们在那段介绍视频里说的，我们是在对话过程中实时做这件事的，而且是以每年一亿次医疗对话的运行规模在做。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we do this in a way that doesn't really break the bank for us?
zh: 我们怎么才能在不把钱包搞破产的前提下做到这一点呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So one place that this problem comes up is actually in generating the clinical note.
zh: 这个问题出现的一个地方，实际上是在生成临床笔记的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when you're generating the clinical note, there's many different sections to it.
zh: 生成临床笔记时，里面有很多不同的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a history of present illness, past medical history, and there's the assessment and plan.
zh: 有现病史、既往病史，还有评估和计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the core insights for us is, rather than, say, using a foundation model to generate all of this, is we can actually decompose this problem into simpler, smaller workflows.
zh: 所以我们的一个核心洞察是，与其用一个基础模型来生成全部这些内容，我们实际上可以把这个问题分解成更简单、更小的工作流。

speaker: Unknown
en: Healthcare is actually many specific workflows.
zh: 医疗保健实际上是由许多具体的工作流组成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need Fable 5 to actually solve all of your clinical nodes.
zh: 你不需要 Fable 5 来解决你所有的临床笔记问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't need frontier-level intelligence for every problem.
zh: 我们不是每个问题都需要前沿级别的智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we actually post-train a lot of smaller models for different problems, such as different actually even to the granularity of different sections in the clinical node.
zh: 所以我们实际上针对不同问题后训练了很多更小的模型，甚至细到临床笔记中不同章节这样的粒度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that lets us use much smaller models because it's a more specific problem and at much cheaper costs and latency.
zh: 这让我们可以使用小得多的模型，因为问题更具体了，而且成本和延迟也便宜得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have this data flywheel.
zh: 而且我们有这个数据飞轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this unique data set of 100 million medical conversations a year.
zh: 我们有这个每年一亿次医疗对话的独特数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as far as we know, no one else has such a large data set.
zh: 据我们所知，没有其他人拥有这么大的数据集。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our key insight is having a right to win in training models.
zh: 所以我们的关键洞察是，在训练模型上拥有制胜权(right to win)。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are problems where the quality is already maxed out.
zh: 有些问题的质量已经到顶了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you should train models then to reduce quality and latency.
zh: 那么这种情况下你训练模型就该是为了降低成本和延迟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are other problems where the quality isn't maxed out and people say, oh, the frontier model would just steamroll you.
zh: 但也有一些问题质量还没到顶，人们会说：哦，前沿模型会直接碾压你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our key insight is we can actually potentially beat the rate of change on the frontier model if we have the right to win by having the right data that they may not have and the focus on a problem that they may not be focusing on.
zh: 我们的关键洞察是，如果我们拥有制胜权——也就是拥有他们可能没有的合适数据，以及聚焦于他们可能没有聚焦的问题——我们实际上有可能跑赢前沿模型的变化速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that lets us still maximize quality.
zh: 这让我们仍然能把质量最大化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another problem that I'll quickly touch on is in-visit orders.
zh: 另一个我会快速讲到的问题是就诊中的医嘱(in-visit orders)。

speaker: Unknown
en: So doctors really aren't big fans of pending orders, but often they'll mention orders during the visit itself, medication or non-medication orders.
zh: 医生们其实不太喜欢待处理的医嘱(pending orders),但他们经常会在就诊过程中提到医嘱，药物或非药物的医嘱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what we have is while we're listening in the visit, as the clinician says order, we actually queue it up in the background and let them actually sign it off in the EHR.
zh: 所以我们的做法是，在就诊中倾听时，当临床医生说出医嘱，我们实际上会在后台把它排队，然后让他们在 EHR 里正式签署确认。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can imagine if we did this in a very naive way, like every few seconds they're just listening for orders, that would really break the bank.
zh: 但你可以想象，如果我们用非常天真的方式做这件事，比如每隔几秒就去监听有没有医嘱，那成本真的会爆炸。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of our tricks are like, how do we find the right events in the conversation to actually trigger heavier models that will actually do the order matching?
zh: 所以我们的很多技巧都是：如何在对话中找到合适的事件，来真正触发那些会去做医嘱匹配的更重的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you need to match the order, not just is the order said, but does it match references to orders that are approved by the system and are relevant to the conversation?
zh: 因为你需要匹配医嘱，不仅仅是医嘱有没有被说到，而是它是否匹配那些被系统批准的、并且与对话相关的医嘱引用。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have a number of different gates that are cheaper and faster that let us trigger actually larger models and hand off to them for actually doing the end-to-end work.
zh: 所以我们有很多不同的、更便宜更快的闸门，让我们能够触发实际上更大的模型，并把工作交接给它们去做端到端的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the last message, this was, of course, a very quick talk, but the message I want to leave you with is healthcare is a domain that needs frontier AI and actually puts it to the higher stakes.
zh: 最后一条信息——当然，这是一个非常简短的演讲——但我想留给你们的信息是：医疗保健是一个需要前沿 AI 的领域，而且真正把它用在了高风险的场景上。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the past, I, as an engineer myself, was worried about working in healthcare.
zh: 过去，我作为一名工程师本人，曾担心在医疗行业工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does healthcare technology actually work?
zh: 医疗技术到底行不行？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, Abridge has proven this at scale, for sure, and hopefully I gave you a taste of some of the frontier problems that we work on.
zh: 嗯，Abridge 肯定已经在大规模上证明了这一点，希望我也让你们尝到了一些我们正在攻克的前沿问题的味道。

speaker: Unknown
en: So thank you so much.
zh: 所以非常感谢大家。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Chaitanya again, and feel free to connect with me at Twitter or LinkedIn.
zh: 我再自我介绍一下，我叫 Chaitanya,欢迎在 Twitter 或 LinkedIn 上与我联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you.
zh: 谢谢。
